objects.original: Corollary 5.16’s projected derivative of an extension of a genuine gradient, specialized to Example 5.17’s polynomial.
objects.reconstructed: The continuous-linear projected derivative of the chosen polynomial.
objects.evidence: In the symmetric finite-Euclidean case these are the same construction. The packet binds a specialization, not a general formalization of the corollary.

domains.original: For x on the finite Euclidean unit sphere, an operator from its orthogonal tangent plane back to that plane.
domains.reconstructed: K=(ℝx)⊥→L[ℝ]K for any real inner-product E and unit x.
domains.evidence: The codomain and domain agree on the source restriction, but the ambient scope is generalized and is not disclosed in the exact declaration lesson or candidate assumptions.

quantifiers.original: Each unit x and each tangent input u for the source symmetric A.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Each unit x and tangent u for each continuous A.
quantifiers.evidence: The definition packages all u into the linear map rather than taking u as a separate theorem binder.

assumptions.original: Smooth genuine gradient extension, symmetric A and finite Euclidean ambient for Example 5.17.
assumptions.reconstructed: Any continuous real-linear A on E. A separate private theorem proves actual smoothness without extra hypotheses.
assumptions.evidence: Projection to the complement of a one-dimensional span requires no ambient completeness. Genuine differentiation is discharged in the module, not added as a binder.

conclusion.original: Hess f(x)[u] equals projected derivative, as a tangent vector.
conclusion.reconstructed: This specific map is P_K ∘ fderiv(G_A,x) ∘ inclusion, with checked differentiability separately.
conclusion.evidence: The body definition matches the source restriction; the evaluation theorem rewrites fderiv using exact HasFDerivAt.

scopes.original: Induced Hessian interpretation in the symmetric finite-dimensional setup; Corollary 5.16 is general but not the object of this definition.
scopes.reconstructed: The exact lesson calls it a Hessian realization without expressly saying that the generic analytic definition is not generally an induced Hessian.
scopes.evidence: For a nonzero skew A acting on the e2,e3 plane and annihilating e1 in ℝ³, F is identically zero but the projected derivative at e1 is nonzero on K.

constant_dependencies.original: x determines the tangent projector; the extension is fixed by A, with normalization inherited from F.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: A, x, and canonical projection of the complement of span{x}; no external gradient field or connection parameter.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The exact #print composes the actual K inclusion, ambient fderiv of the fixed G_A, and projection onto K.
